metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Real-world traffic video frames from which vehicle locations are extracted and reformed as position matrices. Three consecutive frames are used as observation input, with each observation being 4x512 pixels after zooming and down-sampling. Used for simulation experiments.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Data is available from the corresponding author upon request; no direct public link provided.

nodes_process.node_name: Extract vehicle locations from video frames
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations are identified from raw traffic video frames and then converted into position matrices, serving as visual representations of the traffic state.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, 0/3 tools named, 0 params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: For computation efficiency, down-sampling is introduced before the matrix stack to reduce the input dimensions and maintain sufficient information about vehicle positions.
nodes_process.description: To reduce input dimensions for computational efficiency while preserving crucial vehicle position information, the position matrices are down-sampled.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, 0/1 tools named, 0 params stated

nodes_process.node_name: Stack matrices for traffic state representation
nodes_process.source_quote: Since one matrix is insufficient to describe vehicle dynamics, we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state s₁: S₁ = {m₁-(N-1),..., m₁}.
nodes_process.description: Consecutive down-sampled position matrices are stacked to form a comprehensive representation of the traffic state, capturing vehicle dynamics over time. The state s_t is defined as a sequence of N matrices from t-(N-1) to t.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/1 tool named, 1/1 param stated

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: The Q-network architecture is defined, adapted from Mnih et al. [30]. It includes three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and a fully connected (FC) layer for each output layer, as detailed in Figure 7. It also includes a multitask learning strategy for predicting speed and queue length simultaneously.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all parameters stated from Figure 7

nodes_process.source_quote: Initialize the action-value function Q with random weights w.
nodes_process.description: The weights w of the action-value function Q-network are initialized randomly before the training process begins.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, random initialization method not specified

nodes_process.source_quote: Initialize the target network Q-with weights w¯ = w
nodes_process.description: The target network Q- is initialized by copying the randomly initialized weights w from the Q-network.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, direct copy, no specific params

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward r₁ after action at is defined by the following: rt = vt + wqt, μ > 0, ω < 0
nodes_process.description:
The reward function r_t is defined as a linear combination of the average speed v_t in the merging area and the average queue length q_t at the on-ramp, with positive weight 
 for speed and negative weight 
 for queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/1 tool named, 2/2 params stated

nodes_process.source_quote: Fill the replay buffer randomly
nodes_process.description: The replay buffer, which stores data for training, is initially filled with random transitions before the main training loop.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, replay buffer size stated, random fill method not detailed

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1. The ramp meter takes new action with the e-greedy strategy...
nodes_process.description: The Q-network is trained using a deep Q-learning algorithm to learn the optimal ramp metering policy. This involves observing states, choosing actions with an epsilon-greedy strategy, executing actions, obtaining rewards and next states, storing transitions in a replay buffer, sampling mini-batches for training, computing a total loss function (L1 + L2), and updating Q-network weights using Adam. The target network weights are updated periodically.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all params stated, 2/7 tools mentioned (Adam, Mnih et al. for architecture)

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: Traffic scenarios, including the DRL ramp metering method, a no-control scenario, and a PI-ALINEA method, are simulated using the SUMO microscopic traffic simulator. The simulation setup covers an on-ramp, upstream/downstream mainlines, and a merging area.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, SUMO mentioned, 4/5 params stated (traffic volumes implicitly in fig, not param)

nodes_process.source_quote: The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles. The ramp metering rate rk for k-th cycle is given by the following: rk = rk-1 + KR[ok − ô] – Kp[ok-1 − 0k]
nodes_process.description: The PI-ALINEA ramp metering method is implemented, fixing the green phase length and determining the red phase length using a feedback control law based on previous red phase length and downstream occupancies.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/1 tool, all params stated including formula

nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_process.description: The 25th, 50th (median), and 75th percentiles of travel times in the mainline are evaluated and compared across the DRL, PI-ALINEA, and no-control scenarios.

nodes_process.source_quote: The information in the subarea is removed from original data to generate perturbed data for each subarea.
